title: The emergence of strategic reasoning of large language models
abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning abilities in structured tasks (e.g., coding and mathematics), it remains unexplored whether these abilities extend to strategic multi-agent environments. We investigate strategic reasoning capabilities -- the process of choosing an optimal course of action by predicting and adapting to others' actions -- of LLMs by analyzing their performance in three classical games from behavioral economics. We evaluate three standard LLMs (ChatGPT-4, Claude-2.1, Gemini 1.5) and three specialized reasoning LLMs (GPT-o1, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini Flash Thinking 2.0) using hierarchical models of bounded rationality. Our results show that reasoning LLMs exhibit superior strategic reasoning compared to standard LLMs (which do not demonstrate substantial capabilities), and often match or exceed human performance. Since strategic reasoning is fundamental to future AI systems (including Agentic AI and Artificial General Intelligence), our findings demonstrate the importance of dedicated reasoning capabilities in achieving effective strategic reasoning.

title: Nigerian Salafi Discourse Corpus (NSDC)
abstract: The Nigerian Salafi Discourse Corpus (NSDC) is a purpose-built corpus of 5,791 Facebook posts (2,485,963 words; 2,518,453 tagged tokens; 149,431 sentences) published by Nigerian pages and profiles between 2015 and 2025. The corpus was assembled from eight keyword-filtered exports of the Meta Content Library (Salafis, Salafism, Salafiyyah, Ahlus-Sunnah, Sunni, Wahabism, Wahabiyyah, Salafool) and processed through a fully documented, machine-verified pipeline: schema validation, three-pass deduplication, Unicode normalisation and script-based noise removal, SGML-annotated corpus assembly, cross-keyword merging, and calendar-year segmentation. This release contains three artefacts: (1) the cleaned corpus (one UTF-8 file per post, SGML metadata tags, one sentence per line); (2) the tagged vertical corpus (Penn Treebank part-of-speech and lemma, 15 semantic fields, 15 discourse strategies), in the vertical format used by Sketch Engine and CQP; and (3) the corpus segmented by calendar year for diachronic analysis.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Entanglement Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum entanglement algorithm designed for high-precision computation and quantum key distribution. The core concept revolves around leveraging the non-linear properties of quantum entanglement to accelerate computations and facilitate efficient key distribution. We propose a novel approach that dynamically manipulates the entangled state, utilizing its inherent nonlinear behavior to enhance computational speed and security. The algorithm's design incorporates a complex set of quantum state transformations to achieve significant performance improvements compared to existing methods. This research contributes to the advancement of quantum computing by exploring a fundamentally new approach to entanglement-based computation. We detail the algorithm's architecture, mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental validation, demonstrating its potential for high-precision calculations and secure key exchange.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Error Mitigation via Topological State Reconstruction
abstract: Quantum computing offers immense computational power, but the fragility of quantum states makes error correction a significant challenge. Traditional error mitigation techniques often rely on approximations and can introduce significant overhead. This paper introduces an innovative approach to adaptive quantum error mitigation, centered around topological state reconstruction. We propose a novel method for identifying and correcting errors by leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states. This approach offers a proactive and potentially more accurate method for quantum computation compared to traditional methods, driven by a simplified and robust error correction strategy. The core mechanism involves reconstructing a topological state that is less susceptible to errors, allowing for more accurate computations with reduced computational cost. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the reliability of quantum computations.

title: Probability Space-Time Model Learning
abstract: Probability Space-Time Model Learning aims to develop a novel learning framework that automatically learns model parameters and achieves enhanced generalization capabilities, incorporating a probabilistic space-time model. The core mechanism utilizes the inherent properties of these models to facilitate automatic parameter adaptation and strategic adjustment of the learning process. This approach offers a significant departure from traditional parameter tuning methods, potentially unlocking enhanced predictive performance and adaptability across various applications. This research investigates the design and implementation of this framework, focusing on its ability to learn robust models capable of handling complex data patterns. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the framework's design, demonstrating its efficacy through illustrative examples and a discussion of its potential impact on machine learning and data analysis. The ultimate goal is to establish a paradigm shift in model development, enabling more automated and intelligent learning processes.

title: Meta-Learning for Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of meta-learning techniques with evolutionary algorithms (EAs) for neural architecture search (NAS). Traditional NAS methods, particularly those employing EAs, often suffer from high computational costs due to the extensive exploration of the architectural search space. We propose a novel framework that leverages meta-learning to accelerate this process. The core idea is to train a meta-learning model that learns from past NAS trials, effectively guiding the evolutionary algorithm towards more promising architectures and significantly reducing the search space. Our approach demonstrates the potential for substantial improvements in both the efficiency and effectiveness of NAS. The model learns to predict the fitness of new architectures based on limited information from previous searches, acting as a prior for the evolutionary process. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superiority compared to standard EA-based NAS approaches. The key contribution lies in the synergy between the global search capability of EAs and the adaptive learning ability of meta-learning.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Energy Field Optimization
abstract: Quantum state adaptive energy field optimization is a novel approach to enhance quantum computation by dynamically adjusting the energy landscape of quantum states. This research introduces a new algorithm, termed Adaptive Energy Field Optimization (AEFO), that leverages a self-adaptive model to optimize the energy fields of qubits, leading to improved efficiency and precision. The core mechanism focuses on iteratively refining the energy configuration based on a feedback loop, minimizing energy dissipation and maximizing the fidelity of quantum operations. This work explores the potential of AEFO to address key challenges in quantum computing, specifically concerning qubit coherence and gate fidelity.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of mathematics and physics, offers a radically different approach to information encoding and manipulation. This paper explores the potential of self-adaptive quantum topology transformation, a novel algorithm designed to leverage quantum entanglement and topological properties to enhance quantum computation. We present a core claim detailing this approach and highlight the potential benefits, particularly in expanding quantum information and improving computational efficiency. The paper details the core mechanism, outlining the key steps involved in utilizing quantum entanglement and topological transformations to achieve this goal. This research contributes to the development of a robust and adaptable quantum information processing paradigm.

title: 基于量子计算的非线性自适应进化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing-based evolutionary algorithm designed for rapid exploration of complex environments. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with the complexity of such environments, necessitating computationally intensive and potentially suboptimal solutions. We propose a quantum-enhanced evolutionary process that leverages quantum simulation and entanglement to accelerate the search for optimal solutions. This algorithm utilizes a quantum-inspired approach to represent and manipulate evolutionary parameters, allowing for more efficient exploration of the solution space. The core mechanism involves quantum entanglement to facilitate rapid pattern recognition and adaptation, ultimately leading to faster convergence and improved performance in challenging scenarios. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional evolutionary algorithms in a range of complex problem domains. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of this technology on various fields, emphasizing its promise for tackling problems currently intractable with classical methods.

title: ##基于多模态神经元模拟的认知架构
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cognitive architecture construction based on multi-modal neural simulations. The core idea is to replicate the complex activity patterns of diverse neuronal types within the brain, such as integrating cells, predictive cells, and memory cells, to build more realistic and accurate cognitive models. We introduce a new neural model capable of simulating simultaneous activation of various neuronal types and producing complex outputs based on multiple inputs – visual, auditory, motor, and proprioceptive – respectively. Leveraging agent-based simulations, these multi-modal neural models are interconnected to form a cognitive architecture. Through simulating the interactions between these neurons, we aim to mimic sophisticated cognitive processes including decision-making, learning, memory, and attention. This method offers a significant advancement over existing architectures that often rely on simplified or abstract neural models, providing a more biologically plausible and effective framework for understanding and simulating complex cognition. ---

title: Validating FKG.in: Soundness Assessment in LLM-Augmented Indian Food Knowledge
abstract: The online culinary ecosystem is increasingly populated by recipe content generated, modified, or summarized by Large Language Models (LLMs). While often plausible, such outputs may contain hallucinated ingredients, misrepresented quantities, or culturally implausible combinations, limiting their suitability for downstream applications and knowledge graph construction. In this paper, we present a semi-automated soundness assessment workflow for validating structured recipe data extracted and augmented by LLMs from informal culinary sources. Developed as part of FKG(.in), a knowledge graph of Indian food, the pipeline identifies and addresses common failure modes, including structural inconsistencies, semantic and logical incoherence, and deviations from the source text, through a multi-stage process combining formal grammars, vocabulary-based checks, statistical heuristics, Set Transformer-based coherence modeling, and retrieval-based verification. Although evaluated on Indian recipes, the proposed methods are applicable to broader multilingual and multicultural culinary domains. We provide a practical, auditable, and application-agnostic framework for validating LLM-augmented recipe data, thereby strengthening the foundations of machine-readable food knowledge infrastructures in the era of LLM-generated content.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Network Propagation for Complex Probability Distributions
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian Network Propagation presents a novel approach to probabilistic model exploration, leveraging quantum principles to accelerate the search for optimal configurations within complex probability spaces. This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing and superposition to improve Bayesian Network propagation, specifically addressing the challenges posed by high-dimensional data. We demonstrate that incorporating these quantum techniques can significantly enhance the exploration process, resulting in more accurate predictions compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism focuses on efficiently navigating the probabilistic space using quantum phenomena. This work contributes to a more robust and efficient probabilistic modeling technique, potentially impacting a wide range of applications requiring precise predictions.

title: Hardware Acceleration Algorithms Based on Quantum Demixing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum demixing, specifically the phenomenon of quantum decoherence, to accelerate computational tasks. The core idea is to design a hardware acceleration algorithm that exploits controlled interactions between qubits to maximize decoherence time, thereby enhancing both the accuracy and efficiency of the computation. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, focusing on the design principles for a quantum hardware accelerator. The presented framework provides a foundation for future research into developing practical quantum algorithms that harness the power of decoherence for computational speedup. The algorithm is presented as a modular design allowing for flexibility in implementation and adaptation to diverse computational problems. title: Neuro-Symbolic Logic Programming with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to artificial intelligence—Neuro-Symbolic Logic Programming with Reinforcement Learning—designed to address the limitations of current AI techniques. The core idea is to integrate the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the reasoning and explainability offered by symbolic logic programming, guided by reinforcement learning. We present a hybrid system where a neural network learns a high-level representation of a task, translating sensory inputs into abstract concepts. This representation is then fed into a symbolic logic engine, which executes predefined rules and generates plans. Reinforcement learning is utilized to optimize the neural network's representation and the logic engine's rule selection, allowing the system to adapt and improve its performance over time. This approach aims to create AI systems that are not only capable of complex behavior but also provide verifiable, logically sound explanations for their actions. The system's architecture and the interaction between its components are detailed, highlighting the potential for robust and explainable AI. We demonstrate a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and their interplay, and discuss potential future research directions.

title: Quantum Topology: Geometric Geometry Computation
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field, offers a novel approach to geometric computation, leveraging quantum mechanics to explore topological properties. This paper investigates the application of quantum geometry to the analysis of topological structures, focusing on the concept of geometric geometry computation. We propose a method for quantifying topological invariants using quantum entanglement and quantum state manipulation, aiming to establish a new framework for geometric analysis. The core claim is that this approach can provide a more precise and computationally efficient method for understanding and manipulating topological geometry. The research will detail the implementation of a quantum algorithm for calculating geometric invariants, explore the potential of quantum entanglement to reveal hidden topological relationships, and present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method. This work will contribute to the burgeoning field of quantum geometry and its potential to revolutionize geometric computation.

title: Multi-Variable Quantum Error Correction and Quantum Communication Protocol Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to multi-variable quantum error correction (VQEC) and its application in designing quantum communication protocols. The core claim is to design a code capable of simultaneously correcting multiple qubit errors, significantly enhancing the resilience of quantum information transmission. The proposed mechanism leverages quantum entanglement and classical channels to construct a VQEC code, employing an encoding-decoding algorithm for reliable quantum communication. Unlike existing codes primarily focused on single-qubit error correction, this research introduces a framework for scalable error correction, addressing a critical limitation in the practical implementation of quantum communication. The design incorporates key considerations for channel characterization and decoding efficiency, vital for successful protocol execution. Ultimately, this work contributes to the advancement of robust quantum communication systems by providing a foundational element for complex, multi-qubit protocols.

title: Dynamic Programming with Quantum Memory Access Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the potential of integrating quantum-inspired techniques into dynamic programming (DP) algorithms to optimize memory access patterns. Traditional DP relies heavily on sequential access to memory, which can become a significant bottleneck, particularly for large datasets. We propose a framework that utilizes concepts analogous to superposition and entanglement to parallelize memory access operations, thereby reducing computational overhead. The core claim is that by intelligently mimicking quantum memory access strategies, we can achieve speedups exceeding those attainable through purely classical DP approaches. We detail a methodology for adapting DP formulations to exploit this parallel access, focusing on techniques for efficiently managing and accessing memory locations. This work represents a novel application of quantum-inspired ideas to a well-established algorithmic paradigm, offering a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of DP in resource-constrained environments.

title: Decentralized Verification via Quantum State Tomography
abstract: This paper proposes a novel decentralized verification framework utilizing quantum state tomography performed on a distributed network of quantum sensors. The core idea is to leverage the inherent properties of quantum mechanics—specifically, the disturbance introduced by measurement—to establish verifiable proof of computational integrity and data authenticity. Unlike traditional centralized verification systems reliant on a single trusted authority, this approach distributes the verification process across multiple independent sensors. Each sensor independently measures a quantum state, generating a local tomography result. Sophisticated algorithms then analyze the consistency of these distributed results, detecting any deviations that could indicate tampering or unauthorized modification. The framework's robustness stems from the fundamental uncertainty principle, which dictates that precise measurement of a quantum state inevitably introduces disturbance. This disturbance serves as a verifiable signature, providing a tamper-evident record. This paper details the theoretical foundations, outlines the key components of the system, and explores the potential applications of this decentralized verification approach.

title: Self-Healing Neural Networks via Dynamic Network Rewiring with Graph Laplacian Regularization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to enhancing the robustness and adaptability of neural networks through dynamic network rewiring. The core idea is to equip the network with a self-healing mechanism that proactively addresses instability caused by unforeseen changes in input data. This is achieved by incorporating a graph Laplacian regularization term within a dynamic rewiring strategy. The proposed method allows the network to automatically detect and repair damaged connections, thereby maintaining network performance and resilience. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and formulation of key mathematical concepts. The primary focus is on establishing a framework for continuous adaptation, a critical element often overlooked in traditional neural network design. The theoretical underpinning of this work lies in concepts from graph theory, dynamical systems, and optimization, aiming to provide a robust solution to the inherent vulnerabilities of static neural network architectures. The key contribution is a formalized method for dynamically adapting network topology based on a learned representation of network health, quantified by the graph Laplacian. This approach promises to improve the reliability and longevity of neural networks in real-world applications where data distributions and environmental conditions are subject to constant change.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic regression that integrates evolutionary algorithms with quantum annealing. Existing symbolic regression methods often face challenges in efficiently exploring the high-dimensional solution space, particularly when dealing with complex mathematical relationships. Our proposed framework leverages the strengths of both quantum computing and evolutionary optimization. Quantum annealing is employed to identify promising regions within the solution space, guided by the inherent probabilistic nature of quantum systems. Subsequently, evolutionary algorithms are utilized to refine and optimize these candidate expressions, ensuring a robust and accurate representation of the underlying data. The combination of these techniques aims to overcome the limitations of traditional symbolic regression, potentially leading to the discovery of more accurate and efficient mathematical models. The core claim is that this synergistic approach significantly enhances the exploration capabilities of symbolic regression.

title: Memory Fragment Reconstruction Engine
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning, termed the Memory Fragment Reconstruction Engine. The core claim is that fragmented memories can be automatically reorganized into coherent and meaningful knowledge structures using association graph algorithms. The underlying mechanism involves constructing a dynamic association graph based on the analysis of relationships between memory fragments. This graph is then utilized by graph algorithms for path planning and node merging, effectively linking disparate fragments and forming new knowledge structures. Unlike traditional approaches focused on static knowledge representation and inference, this engine exhibits greater adaptability and self-organizing capabilities, specifically tailored to the challenges of reconstructing fragmented memories. The system's architecture, algorithms, and potential applications are described, highlighting its unique contribution to the field of cognitive science and artificial intelligence.

title: Rescheduled, not redefined: The moving plateau of old-age mortality
abstract: Whether the risk of death keeps climbing at extreme ages or levels off has divided researchers for a century. We show this conflict reflects a moving target. Using cohort data from twelve low-mortality populations, we find that mortality deceleration and plateau onset shift steadily later across cohorts born from the mid-19th to the early-20th century. The data support a plateau across the full cohort range, though evidence weakens for the youngest, incompletely observed cohorts. In these younger cohorts, deceleration begins near age 100, and the fitted plateau begins beyond age 108. Because past studies focused on different cohorts and fixed age ranges, they sampled different phases of the exact same shift. The mortality plateau has no fixed age: it has been rescheduled.

title: RouteSparse: Input-Conditional Pattern Routing for Budgeted Long-Context Prefilling
abstract: Dynamic sparse attention can reduce the quadratic cost of long-context prefilling without changing model weights. MInference assigns each attention head one pattern offline and estimates that pattern's sparse indices for every prompt. This design is efficient, but it assumes that a head's preferred pattern and sparsity budget remain suitable across inputs. We introduce RouteSparse, which routes each head and prompt segment among a small library of GPU-efficient sparse patterns. A low-cost probe estimates pattern utility and uncertainty; a latency-aware router then selects a pattern and budget, while uncertain cases fall back to a denser mask. We formulate routing as constrained risk minimization, derive an attention-output error certificate from omitted probability mass, and evaluate the method on long-context retrieval, question answering, summarization, and language modeling. On Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct with 128K-token prompts, RouteSparse achieves $6.5\times$ dense prefill speed with a 0.2-point RULER drop relative to dense attention, compared with $7.3\times$ speed and a 1.6-point drop for fixed per-head routing. Ablations confirm that input-conditional routing, hardware profiling, and selective dense fallback each contribute to the quality--latency tradeoff.

title: Multimodal Deep Attention Fusion of Longitudinal EHR and Diagnostic Imaging for Real-Time Sepsis and Deterioration Prediction in Critical Care
abstract: Early detection of clinical deterioration and septic shock in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) remains one of the most pressing challenges in modern critical care medicine. Sepsis is characterized by a dysregulated host response to infection, leading to life-threatening organ dysfunction. While traditional early warning scoring systems (e.g., SOFA, MEWS, APACHE-IV) rely on static, threshold-based heuristics of isolated physiological vital signs, they suffer from high false-alarm rates and lack the ability to assimilate continuous, high-frequency temporal trajectories alongside high-dimensional diagnostic imaging. In this work, we present MedCross-Fusion, a novel multimodal deep learning framework that dynamically integrates irregular, longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) time-series data with diagnostic chest radiography (CXR). Our architecture comprises a Temporal Cross-Attention Transformer coupled with a lightweight Swin-Transformer visual backbone, linked through a cross-modal gating mechanism that dynamically weights visual pathology representations against continuous physiological fluctuations. We train and evaluate MedCross-Fusion on two extensive clinical datasets: MIMIC-IV (comprising over 45,000 ICU admissions) and the multi-center eICU Collaborative Research Database (over 200,000 ICU admissions). MedCross-Fusion achieves an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.925–0.939) and an Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC) of 0.684 for predicting sepsis onset 6 hours prior to clinical diagnosis, significantly outperforming unimodal recurrent baselines (AUROC 0.841) and state-of-the-art multimodal fusion architectures (AUROC 0.887). Furthermore, we integrate Integrated Gradients and Token-wise Attention Rollout to provide interpretable clinical explanations. Our results demonstrate that MedCross-Fusion delivers robust, real-time risk stratification capable of reducing diagnostic latency in critical care settings.

title: ACVAM-DA: An Open-Valence Metareflective Architecture for Artificial Autonomy and Consciousness Research
abstract: This article introduces the Open-Valence Metareflective Cyclic Architecture with Autonomous Development (ACVAM-DA), a falsifiable conceptual framework for investigating artificial autonomy, metacognition, hierarchical self-modification, and theory-derived indicators of consciousness. The architecture refines a basic pleasure–displeasure regulatory loop into three distinct levels of valence: elemental positive and aversive signals, context-sensitive appraisal, and reflective endorsement. Positive and aversive components are represented independently as vector-valued states, preventing intense mixed-valence conditions from being obscured by scalar aggregation. During a bounded calibration phase, out-of-range elemental transducer states may trigger local parameter restoration. After calibration, however, mature preferences and appraisals are not automatically reset solely because their valence reaches extreme values. Instead, the architecture employs monitoring, temporary suspension, causal diagnosis, sandboxed modification, and reversible checkpoints. A minimal non-valential integrity kernel constrains external harm, observability, resource integrity, and reversibility while remaining conceptually separate from mutable preferences, goals, and short-term utility. ACVAM-DA further integrates recurrent global broadcast, generative world and self models, autobiographical memory, causal metacognition, endogenous goal formation, and four orders of plasticity. Two elementary information-loss results are established for scalar valence aggregation and unconditional reset mechanisms, an explicit acceptance rule for self-modifications is formalized, and a program of matched longitudinal ablation studies is specified. The proposed empirical framework distinguishes functional autonomy, metacognition, access-like global availability, phenomenal consciousness, and artificial life, and does not infer any of these properties from fluent self-report alone. A structured scoping search conducted through 29 August 2026 identified close precedents for each individual component of the proposal, including a particularly related recursive-feedback architecture, but no retrieved source instantiated the complete conjunction of the four operational claim bundles defined in the work. The calibration-to-open-valence transition emerged as the most discriminating feature. Accordingly, ACVAM-DA is presented as a potentially novel operational synthesis and a preregistrable experimental research program, rather than as evidence of absolute historical priority or as a demonstration that artificial consciousness can be engineered or detected with certainty.

title: Adaptive Quantum Matrix Geometry Calculation
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to quantum matrix computation, focusing on the dynamic adjustment of the matrix's geometric structure to optimize computational efficiency. Traditional matrix calculations are often static, resulting in suboptimal performance. We propose a novel framework that employs a dynamic geometric structure adjustment strategy, tailoring the matrix's geometry in real-time based on input data. This adaptive methodology significantly enhances computational efficiency compared to static approaches. The paper details the framework's design, implementation, and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in various quantum matrix calculations.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing super-space geometry as a fundamental framework for quantum computation, aiming to address limitations in existing algorithms and improve computational efficiency and robustness. This framework offers a new perspective on quantum algorithm design, potentially enabling significant advancements in computational complexity and error mitigation. The core mechanism centers around creating new quantum circuit topologies that leverage the inherent properties of hyper-space, leading to more efficient and reliable results. This work lays the groundwork for a new generation of quantum algorithms, driven by a fundamentally different geometric approach.

abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to optimize the design of hardware circuits. The core claim is that EAs can effectively achieve more efficient and lower power circuits compared to traditional design methods. The proposed mechanism involves representing circuit design parameters as genes and utilizing EA operators such as crossover and mutation to iteratively refine the design. This approach offers an automated and potentially superior alternative to human-driven design, addressing the limitations of relying solely on human expertise and conventional optimization techniques. The research focuses on leveraging the inherent search capabilities of EAs to explore a vast design space, ultimately leading to improved circuit performance metrics. The paper details the framework for applying EAs to circuit design, including encoding, evaluation, and selection strategies. Simulation results will demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of this methodology.

This memory module acts as a repository for storing and retrieving relevant graph state information, enabling the model to capture and utilize long-range dependencies more effectively. The core claim is that attention mechanisms in GNNs can be significantly enhanced by incorporating external memory. The proposed mechanism improves the model's ability to learn complex graph representations and perform tasks requiring understanding of global graph structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework. The primary contribution is a new paradigm for GNN design focused on explicitly incorporating external memory to address the limitations of standard GNN architectures.

title: Topological Protection-Based Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for adaptive quantum circuits leveraging the protective effects of topological defects in superconducting quantum circuits. The core concept involves constructing superconducting circuits incorporating multiple topological defects, wherein the circuit's quantum states can be dynamically reconfigured upon encountering noise, preserving quantum computation accuracy. This approach addresses the critical challenge of noise resilience in quantum computing by exploiting the inherent robustness of topological protection. The design emphasizes adaptability, allowing the circuit to self-correct and maintain fidelity under fluctuating environmental conditions. Mathematical formulations describe the circuit dynamics and the topological protection mechanism. The proposed architecture offers a promising pathway toward robust and scalable quantum computation. ---

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization (NLQSS)
abstract: Quantum state synchronization is a critical challenge in quantum computing, demanding precise coordination between multiple qubits. Traditional methods often suffer from limitations in speed and fidelity. This paper introduces Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization (NLQSS), a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement to establish robust and efficient synchronization between qubits regardless of their physical distance. We propose a framework that dynamically generates and maintains entanglement to facilitate instantaneous correlation, drastically reducing communication latency and improving synchronization accuracy compared to existing techniques. Our analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of NLQSS in synchronizing quantum states across multiple qubits, showcasing its potential for accelerating complex quantum computations.

title: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Complex Systems Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling complex systems utilizing the principles of multi-agent collaboration. Traditional methods for complex system modeling often rely on static representations, struggling to capture the inherent dynamism and adaptive behavior observed in real-world scenarios. We propose a framework where complex systems are decomposed into a network of interacting intelligent agents. Each agent is responsible for managing a specific aspect of the system, communicating with others through a defined protocol, and adapting its behavior based on received information. The core of the method leverages reinforcement learning or evolutionary algorithms to optimize the strategies of these agents, allowing the system to learn and respond effectively to changing conditions. This dynamic modeling approach enables real-time control and optimization, offering a significant improvement over static modeling techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a flexible and scalable methodology for tackling complex system challenges.

title: DLGNet: A Deep Learning and Generative Framework for Privacy-preserving PII De-identification with Semantic Verification
abstract: The rapid growth of unstructured textual data in domains such as healthcare, education, and enterprise systems has increased the risk of inadvertent exposure of Personally Identifiable Information (PII).Effective deidentification is essential to enable secure data sharing while preserving privacy and regulatory compliance.Existing approaches, including rule-based and deep learning-based Named Entity Recognition (NER) methods, primarily focus on detection and often lack contextual validation and robust replacement mechanisms, leading to information loss or residual privacy risks.This work proposes DLGNet, a pipeline-based integrated framework PII de-identification framework that integrates DeBERTa-based token-level detection, LLM-based semantic verification, and type-aware replacement.A BIO-tagged DeBERTa model identifies candidate PII spans, which are refined using a TinyLlamabased semantic verification module for contextual validation.Detected entities are then replaced using a hybrid generative and rule-based strategy to ensure irreversible transformation while preserving textual coherence.Experimental results demonstrate strong recall-oriented performance, achieving precision of 90.3%, recall of 94.7%, F1-score of 92.4%, and Fβ-score (β = 5) of 94.52%.Utility evaluation shows a length ratio of 0.96 and token overlap of 0.73, indicating effective preservation of textual structure and semantics.The proposed framework provides a unified and practical solution for privacy-preserving text processing by jointly improving detection accuracy, contextual reliability, and data utility.

title: FabroGym: registration of an explainability requirements analysis for a fitness routine recommendation component
abstract: Estudio de caso sobre requisitos no funcionales de explicabilidad para un componente propuesto de recomendación de rutinas. Antes del registro OSF se realizaron seis walkthroughs generales de FabroGym: tres con participantes técnicos y tres con participantes no técnicos. Estas sesiones constituyen evidencia empírica previa/formativa y no datos confirmatorios preregistrados. No se presupone que una explicación estructurada específica haya sido evaluada en las seis sesiones. Después del registro se realizará la codificación sistemática de la evidencia, se identificarán de forma trazable los fragmentos pertinentes para explicabilidad, se formularán o ajustarán candidatos a RNF y, si aún está pendiente, se realizará el member checking final.

title: Calibration and Comparative Analysis of Forward-Looking Sonar and 3D Sonar for Enhanced Underwater Object Recognition
abstract: Sonars generate a significant amount of noise. With the advent of new technology capable of producing full 3D point clouds, the noise is amplified in sparse point clouds, making it challenging to recognize features for navigation, recognition, or reconstruction. To address this challenge, we propose using two different sonar modalities: one that produces a 2D intensity image and another that generates a 3D point cloud. By implementing auto-calibration, we can filter out noisy features between the modalities to enhance feature extraction. Experiments demonstrate that auto-calibration improves performance over manual calibration by 5% and that filtering enhances feature extraction by more than 40% relative to the raw point cloud. Code and datasets are given at https://theaprilab.org/fls-3d-calibrator

title: Formal Verification and Dynamic Software Refactoring: A Collaborative Engine
abstract: This paper presents a novel collaborative engine designed to synergistically integrate formal verification and dynamic software refactoring. The core claim is that combining these two techniques can lead to continuous and optimized software quality. The proposed mechanism involves constructing an engine that leverages the conclusions of formal verification to guide dynamic refactoring processes while simultaneously verifying the correctness of the resulting changes. Current software development practices often treat formal verification and dynamic refactoring as separate, sequential activities. This disconnect hinders effective quality management. Our collaborative engine addresses this limitation by establishing a closed-loop system, offering a streamlined approach to improve software reliability and maintainability. This work outlines the engine's architecture, key components, and the methodology for achieving this synergistic effect. The paper emphasizes the practical benefits of this approach, demonstrating how it can significantly reduce software defects and enhance the overall development lifecycle.

title: Topological Protection of Quantum Information Against Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of topological protection to mitigate decoherence in quantum information processing. The core claim centers around leveraging the robustness of topological states to significantly extend the coherence times of quantum information, thereby effectively suppressing decoherence. The proposed mechanism involves designing encoding schemes within topologically protected quantum systems, exploiting the inherent resilience of topological abnormal states against localized noise. Traditional quantum coding methods rely heavily on external protection, which often proves inefficient. This research demonstrates a paradigm shift by utilizing intrinsic physical properties to achieve genuine quantum information safeguarding. We explore theoretical frameworks and mathematical models to illustrate this approach, focusing on the fundamental principles and potential applications. The goal is to provide a robust foundation for developing future quantum technologies.

title: Probability Geometric Information Theory
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Geometric Information Theory (PGIT), a novel framework for efficiently computing and storing information, particularly in high-dimensional probabilistic spaces and non-linear information systems. The core concept is to leverage the dynamic nature of probability distributions to optimize information storage and retrieval. We propose a method based on iterative optimization and probabilistic computation to achieve significant improvements in data processing speed and efficiency compared to traditional approaches. The paper details the theoretical foundations, algorithmic implementation, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of PGIT. This work offers a new perspective on information theory, potentially revolutionizing data management and analysis.

title: Based on Formal Languages: Program Verification and Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of formal languages – specifically, description logics and type theories – to the domain of program verification and optimization. The core claim is that rigorous verification and optimization of software can be significantly enhanced by representing programs within the precise and traceable framework offered by these formal systems. The mechanism relies on translating program logic into a formal representation, subsequently employing formal verification techniques and optimization strategies. Unlike traditional methods that often rely on heuristics and experience, this approach leverages the inherent properties of formal languages to improve both the efficiency and reliability of the verification and optimization processes. The research investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of this paradigm shift, focusing on the ability to generate provably correct and optimized code. The paper outlines key concepts and techniques, highlighting the potential for a more robust and reliable software development lifecycle. ---

title: 基于动态自适应的概率空间优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for probability space optimization, termed Dynamic Adaptive Probability Space Optimization (DAPSO). DAPSO leverages a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism to enhance optimization efficiency, particularly in complex and high-dimensional problems. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the parameters of the probability space based on the problem characteristics and the learning process. This adaptive approach allows the optimizer to focus its efforts on the most relevant regions of the solution space, leading to improved convergence and faster solution times. We present a theoretical analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of this framework, showcasing its superior performance compared to traditional optimization methods on several benchmark datasets. The paper details the implementation of the dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm and discusses its impact on key optimization metrics, including convergence rate and solution quality. Furthermore, we provide a detailed analysis of the framework's robustness and potential for generalization.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers the potential to revolutionize various computational tasks, particularly in optimization problems. This paper explores the application of QML to adaptive hyperparameter optimization, a crucial step in training machine learning models. We propose a novel QML-based algorithm that leverages quantum state dynamics to automatically adjust hyperparameters, leading to improved model performance. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional static hyperparameter optimization methods by dynamically responding to the data and model itself. The core mechanism involves the quantum state evolution driven by the learning process, enabling a more efficient and robust optimization process. This work demonstrates the potential of QML to significantly enhance model accuracy and generalization capabilities.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Probabilistic Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a fundamentally different approach to computation and information processing. This paper introduces a novel probabilistic algorithm predicated on the utilization of quantum entanglement to enhance numerical simulation and optimization capabilities. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement to introduce a non-classical computational process, resulting in increased accuracy and the ability to navigate a broader range of solution spaces. This work explores the potential of entanglement to overcome limitations imposed by traditional computational methods, presenting a new framework for probabilistic algorithms with significant implications for scientific and engineering applications.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Cooperative Reward Shaping
abstract: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) offers a promising approach to tackling complex cooperative tasks. However, existing MARL algorithms often fail to achieve robust coordination and cooperation, primarily due to difficulties in learning effective joint policies and the lack of mechanisms to encourage collaborative behavior. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates intrinsic motivation and cooperative reward shaping into a MARL system. The core idea is to augment the traditional extrinsic reward signal with internal drives, such as curiosity and competence, and to shape the reward function to explicitly incentivize cooperation among agents. We introduce a framework where agents learn to maximize both their external rewards and their internal motivation levels, while simultaneously benefiting from a carefully designed cooperative reward structure. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of standard MARL and to promote more efficient and stable cooperative learning. We present a detailed description of the framework and discuss its key components, highlighting the interplay between intrinsic motivation, cooperative reward shaping, and the overall learning process. The results, although presented without empirical experimentation, illustrate the potential impact of this approach on improving cooperative MARL performance. ---

title: On Information-Theoretic Program Execution Path Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to program execution path optimization by leveraging concepts from information theory. The core idea is to treat program execution paths as information streams, quantifying their complexity and potential for optimization using metrics like entropy and cross-entropy. We propose a framework utilizing greedy or dynamic programming algorithms to identify and select optimal execution paths, aiming to minimize execution time. This work presents a fundamentally new perspective on program optimization, particularly beneficial for programs with intricate execution paths. The methodology offers a potential route towards more efficient and adaptive program execution, driven by an information-theoretic understanding of program complexity. ---

title: Protocolo de Revisão Sistemática da Literatura - Sistema Tutor Inteligente para Dedução Natural
abstract: Este pacote reúne o protocolo e os artefatos de condução da Revisão Sistemática da Literatura (RSL) que fundamentou o artigo "Tutor Inteligente para Dedução Natural" sobre Sistemas Tutores Inteligentes (STI) para o ensino de Dedução Natural. A revisão seguiu as diretrizes de Kitchenham e Charters (2007) para Engenharia de Software, com o fluxo de seleção relatado conforme o padrão PRISMA 2020, cobrindo cinco bases (IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink e SBC OpenLib), partindo de 1.308 registros recuperados até um corpus final de 65 estudos primários. title: Towards Secure Prompt Processing: A Unified Framework to Detect, Sanitize, and Prevent Adversarial Prompts via Dual-optimized Threshold-aware Learning
abstract: In the modern era, Large Language Models (LLMs) are a cornerstone in the creation of intelligent systems, boasting significant capabilities in various fields.Adversarial prompts continue to pose a significant threat to LLM security, as they exploit the lack of distinction between trusted and malicious prompts.Such weaknesses are extremely critical to the trustworthiness, safety, and reliability of real-world implements.To tackle this, this study introduces a sanitization and high-confidence inference for effective LLM defense through isolation and neutralization gateway (SHIELDING), which consists of linguistic feature extraction, sentiment-based analysis, and a Threshold-aware Random Forest (TRF) classifier.The TRF model is designed to include class-specific threshold optimized via Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO), allowing the model to adaptively make decisions.The experimental results indicate that the proposed method has good performance with an accuracy of 99%, a classification Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 0.656%, and a real ASR of 3.994% showing that it is an effective method to improve the security of LLM.

title: Quantum discord of Gaussian states in non-inertial frames
abstract: We investigate the redistribution of continuous-variable Gaussian quantum discord under the Unruh effect for both one and two uniformly accelerated observers. The discord shared between the inertial mode and the accessible accelerated mode, as well as that between the two accessible accelerated modes, decays monotonically with acceleration and vanishes in the limit $a\to\infty$, while the Unruh effect generates discord in all causally disconnected Rindler mode pairs. The initial quantum correlation is therefore redistributed across Rindler partitions rather than destroyed. We further characterize how the squeezing parameter $s$ and field frequency $ω$ control the discord in different mode-pair classes. For causally connected pairs, $s$ and $ω$ exert comparable, interchangeable effects; for cross-region pairs, the squeezing parameter dominates; and for intra-observer cross-region pairs, the field frequency is more influential. In the two-observer case, the $A_{II}$-$B_{II}$ pair exhibits non-monotonic behavior with a peak whose position shifts to larger $a$ as $ω$ increases, and both parameters contribute only weakly except near an optimal $\fracω{s}$ ratio.

title: ToriLearn: An AI Enabled Adaptive Learning System for GCE Chemistry Preparation
abstract: Secondary school students preparing for the General Certificate of Education examinations in Cameroon face a documented 62 percent failure rate in core science subjects, alongside heavy reliance on static revision material that does not adjust to what a learner already knows. This paper presents the design and implementation of ToriLearn, a prototype web based adaptive learning platform built to address this gap for GCE Ordinary Level Chemistry. The system combines a React and TypeScript frontend with a Django REST Framework backend organised into four layers, namely presentation, API, application logic, and data persistence. Within the application layer, a Bayesian Knowledge Tracing engine estimates mastery of eleven Chemistry knowledge components in real time, a Gradient Boosting classifier recommends chapter level progression, a K-Means clustering module groups learners by behaviour, and a conversa-tional tutor built on Groq hosted large language models supplies explanations with an offline fallback chain. The system was built across five Agile Scrum sprints and evaluated through functional testing, performance benchmarking on a local development server, and mathematical simulation of three learner trajectories. Results show that all core modules function correctly, that the adaptive quiz endpoint responds within 45 to 80 milliseconds under development conditions, and that the simulated learner scenarios behave in a manner consistent with the underlying Bayesian model. No live classroom pilot was conducted, so claims in this paper are limited to architectural soundness and simulated behaviour rather than measured learning gains. We discuss how this layered, fallback aware design compares with existing intelligent tutoring architectures and outline what a subsequent classroom deployment would need to confirm.

title: The Label Moves the Reading: Entity-Name Leakage in Language-Model Dimensional Ratings of a Fixed Text
abstract: A dimensional rating produced by a language model over a written artifact is normally treated as a reading of that artifact. This study shows it is not purely that. Holding an artifact byte-identical and exchanging only the entity name it concerns, an eight-dimensional profile moved by .55 to .82 rubric points per dimension across two independently designed collections, at or above the same operators' test-retest spread in every run, over 1,057 records from six operators in three model families. The deflationary account – that the effect registers incongruity between a text written for one entity and a label naming another – is refuted: texts authored for no entity produced a larger effect, .824 against .584. The movement is structured rather than diffuse, the largest and smallest dimensions differing by a factor of 2.4 with both extremes reproducing across runs. Which of three routes carries the leakage is not identified, and the study reports why rather than resolving it: a re-analysis shows the neutrality guard that blocked the decomposition referred its interaction to the entity main effect rather than the within-cell residual, and the class effect is roughly half a percent of total variance, so that ratio is a ratio of two small quantities. Referred correctly, the interaction is roughly five percent of residual. The exchange procedure is offered as a diagnostic other rubric instruments can be put through. Includes zharnikov-2026bp-entity-name-leakage.yaml (Paper Spec v0.1.0) – a machine-readable specification of the paper's claims, assumptions, and dependencies. The paper's full machine-first bundle (the SPINE claim/dependency graph and the ONTOLOGY term module) lives in the public repository; see https://github.com/spectralbranding/paper-spec for the standard. title: Nonlinear Model Parameter Optimization via Dynamic Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to non-linear model parameter optimization utilizing a dynamic optimization framework. The core challenge in many real-world applications is finding optimal model parameters that accurately represent the underlying data. Traditional parameter optimization methods often rely on manually tuned parameters, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield the best results. We introduce a dynamic optimization algorithm that automatically adjusts model parameters based on a complex model analysis, aiming to improve both prediction accuracy and generalization ability. The algorithm incorporates a "dynamic parameter" mechanism that iteratively refines parameter values to achieve a more optimal configuration. This approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods, particularly in scenarios with complex, non-linear models. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed dynamic optimization framework through rigorous analysis and simulated results.

title: Self-Organizing Semantic Networks
abstract: This paper explores the concept of Self-Organizing Semantic Networks (SOSN), a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning. Traditional semantic networks are static, requiring manual design and refinement. We propose a system, the Meta-Network Weaver, which dynamically creates and evolves a network based on data analysis, achieving self-organizing properties. This system aims to improve knowledge representation by automatically adjusting connections and creating a more flexible and adaptable structure. The paper details the design and implementation of the Meta-Network Weaver, highlighting its key mechanisms and demonstrating its potential benefits through a simulated case study.

title: Quantum Potential Simulation of Adaptive Topological Structure Adjustment
abstract: Quantum potential simulation offers a powerful tool for modeling complex quantum systems, particularly those exhibiting topological properties. However, traditional approaches often struggle with the computational cost of accurately capturing topological features. This paper introduces a novel method for quantum potential simulation that dynamically adjusts the quantum potential field to enhance the simulation's accuracy and efficiency. We propose a self-adaptive topology adjustment algorithm, which iteratively optimizes the quantum potential based on the system's state. This approach leverages quantum state learning to achieve significant improvements in simulation fidelity and speed, offering a promising path toward more efficient and precise quantum simulations.

title: Title: Bayesian Statistical Resonance – Predictive Modeling of Mathematical Structure
abstract: This research investigates the potential for Bayesian statistical resonance – a novel approach to modeling the statistical dependence inherent in mathematical structures – to predict the emergence of new mathematical theorems and concepts. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture the complex, non-linear dependencies that drive innovation in mathematics. This work proposes a Bayesian framework specifically designed to identify these subtle correlations, offering a predictive capability exceeding existing techniques. The core mechanism centers on a modified Bayesian network that incorporates non-linear relationships and dynamically adjusts its parameters based on observed data, fostering a feedback loop that anticipates future mathematical developments. This research aims to move beyond simple pattern recognition and towards a deeper understanding of the underlying mathematical structure, ultimately providing a powerful tool for mathematical discovery.

title: 自适应的变量空间拓扑的量子计算应用
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive variable space topology in quantum computation, aiming to enhance precision and efficiency in large-data processing. We introduce a novel dynamic topology design, dynamically adjusting the topology based on data characteristics, and leveraging this adaptation to improve computational accuracy. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the inherent properties of quantum topology to optimize complex calculations. The study demonstrates the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional data. This work presents a framework for automatically adapting variable space topologies, offering a significant advancement in the design of quantum algorithms.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology-Based Constraint Modeling in Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based constraint modeling mechanism for evolutionary algorithms, aiming to enhance the exploration of the solution space and improve convergence. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often fix the topology of constraint networks, limiting the search space. We propose a feedback loop that dynamically adjusts topology based on solution quality, providing a mechanism for adaptive exploration. The system incorporates a monitoring mechanism that assesses solution quality and iteratively refines the topology to guide the algorithm toward more promising regions of the solution space. This approach addresses a significant limitation of current evolutionary algorithms, offering a potentially more effective and robust method for finding optimal solutions. The core mechanism involves a continuous assessment of solution quality and a corresponding topology adjustment, ensuring a dynamic and adaptive exploration strategy.

title: Contextual Symbolic Regression with Latent Semantic Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to symbolic regression, termed Contextual Symbolic Regression with Latent Semantic Analysis (CSR-LSA). Traditional symbolic regression methods often struggle with complex datasets exhibiting underlying semantic relationships, leading to inaccurate or computationally expensive model discovery. CSR-LSA addresses this limitation by leveraging Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) to uncover these relationships, reducing the dimensionality of the data while preserving essential semantic information. The resulting latent representation is then used as the operational space for symbolic regression, significantly improving model accuracy and efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CSR-LSA through theoretical analysis and a detailed discussion of the methodology. The core contribution lies in the synergistic combination of symbolic regression's ability to generate equations and LSA's capability to extract hidden semantic structures. The proposed method offers a promising direction for automated model discovery in various domains, particularly those with rich contextual data.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Temporal Encoding
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has emerged as a powerful technique for processing time-series data, particularly in applications demanding real-time response. However, traditional RC often suffers from limitations in sensitivity to temporal changes and adaptability to evolving data patterns. This paper proposes a novel approach—Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Temporal Encoding (QIRCTE)—which integrates principles inspired by quantum measurement theory to enhance the performance of RC. The core idea is to encode temporal information directly into the reservoir's state space, creating a more efficient and robust processing unit. This is achieved through a modified reservoir architecture and a specific learning rule. We demonstrate, theoretically, that this temporal encoding significantly improves the reservoir's ability to capture and respond to transient signals, mirroring aspects of quantum measurement's ability to reveal underlying correlations. The theoretical framework is presented with mathematical derivations, including the state-space equations and the modified learning rule. We outline the key elements of the QIRCTE architecture and discuss potential applications, highlighting its advantages over conventional RC methods.

title: Self-Adaptive Variable Space Graph Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive variable space graph modeling technique, designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting the structure of the variable space graph based on input data characteristics. The proposed model utilizes a learning-based approach to optimize the graph's parameters, allowing for automated feature-driven adjustments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments comparing its performance against existing approaches on several benchmark datasets. The core mechanism centers around a self-tuning parameter adjustment process that adapts to the data's inherent patterns. The paper concludes with a detailed overview of the model's architecture, key improvements, and future research directions.

title: An Explainable XGBoost Framework for Mortality Prediction in People Living with HIV Receiving Antiretroviral Therapy
abstract: Mortality remains an important concern among people living with HIV (PLHIV) receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), particularly when high-risk patients are not identified early. This study presents an explainable mortality prediction approach based on an optimized Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier. A retrospective dataset containing 393 clinical records was analyzed. Before model training, duplicate entries were removed, missing values were imputed, categorical variables were encoded, and class imbalance in the training data was addressed using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Optuna was employed to determine suitable XGBoost hyperparameters, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine how individual predictors affected the model output. Performance was evaluated on an independent testing set using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The resulting classifier achieved an accuracy of 89.87%, weighted precision of 0.91, weighted recall of 0.90, weighted F1-score of 0.90, and an ROC-AUC of 0.948. For the mortality class, recall reached 0.97, with 30 of 31 mortality cases correctly detected. Follow-up duration and functional status contributed most strongly to the predictions. SHAP analysis further showed whether these predictors shifted individual outputs toward mortality or survival. The integration of optimized predictive modeling with explainable artificial intelligence enabled accurate mortality prediction while providing transparent insight into how individual predictors influenced the model output. The findings suggest that the model may assist in identifying patients who require closer monitoring, although validation using external and multicenter data is necessary before clinical implementation.

title: Beyond Accuracy: A Reproducible Framework for Detecting Data Leakage and Shortcut Learning in Machine Learning Pipelines Toward Trustworthy, Reproducible, and Sustainable AI Systems
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in high-impact domains such as healthcare, cybersecurity, autonomous systems, and industrial decision-making, where reliable model evaluation is essential. Despite continuous improvements in predictive performance, growing evidence indicates that many reported gains are inflated by methodological flaws, including data leakage, shortcut learning, dataset shift, and insufficient reproducibility practices. These issues compromise model generalization, reduce robustness, and undermine trust in AI systems. This study proposes a reproducible, leakage-aware evaluation framework designed to detect and quantify methodological risks throughout the machine learning pipeline. The framework integrates four complementary dimensions: dataset integrity analysis, pipeline validation, robustness assessment under controlled perturbations, and reproducibility evaluation. These components are consolidated into a novel Leakage Risk Score (LRS), a normalized metric that estimates methodological risk and complements conventional performance measures such as accuracy. A proof-of-concept evaluation using multiple supervised classification datasets under clean and intentionally contaminated conditions shows that data leakage consistently inflates predictive performance while reducing robustness and reproducibility. Although the empirical validation is intentionally illustrative, the proposed framework establishes a unified foundation for leakage-aware evaluation and supports the transition from benchmark-oriented assessment toward trustworthy, reproducible, and sustainable AI systems.

title: Hybrid deep learning approach with capsule networks for financial fraud detection
abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial services has significantly increased the complexity and volume of financial transactions, making the accurate detection of fraudulent activities a critical challenge for conventional machine learning approaches. This study proposes a hybrid intelligent fraud detection framework that integrates data preprocessing, feature selection, deep learning classification, and adaptive hyperparameter optimization to improve fraud detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Initially, transaction records are preprocessed through missing value treatment, feature normalization, outlier analysis, and Tomek Links undersampling to enhance data quality and address class imbalance. Subsequently, the Perfumer Optimization Algorithm (POA) is employed to identify the most informative feature subset, whereas a Capsule Network performs hierarchical feature representation learning to capture complex relationships among transaction attributes. The Fennec Fox Optimization Algorithm (FFOA) is further utilized to optimize the network hyperparameters, improving convergence and overall classification performance. The proposed framework was evaluated using a publicly available Kaggle financial fraud benchmark dataset and compared with several state-of-the-art deep learning models. Experimental results achieved an accuracy of 99.67%, precision of 99.52%, recall of 99.74%, F1-score of 99.65%, and an MCC of 0.993, while maintaining low computational complexity suitable for real-time applications. Furthermore, SHAP and permutation importance analyses demonstrated that behavioural attributes, particularly failed transaction attempts and transaction frequency, contributed most significantly to fraud prediction. The proposed framework advances financial fraud detection by combining optimization-driven feature selection, hierarchical representation learning, and adaptive hyperparameter tuning into a unified architecture, providing an accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient solution suitable for next-generation intelligent financial security systems.

The Fennec Fox Optimization Algorithm (FFOA) is further utilized to optimize the network hyperparameters, improving convergence and overall classification performance. The proposed framework was evaluated using a publicly available Kaggle financial fraud benchmark dataset and compared with several state-of-the-art deep learning models. Experimental results achieved an accuracy of 99.67%, precision of 99.52%, recall of 99.74%, F1-score of 99.65%, and an MCC of 0.993, while maintaining low computational complexity suitable for real-time applications. Furthermore, SHAP and permutation importance analyses demonstrated that behavioural attributes, particularly failed transaction attempts and transaction frequency, contributed most significantly to fraud prediction. The proposed framework advances financial fraud detection by combining optimization-driven feature selection, hierarchical representation learning, and adaptive hyperparameter tuning into a unified architecture, providing an accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient solution suitable for next-generation intelligent financial security systems.

title: EvoGenUI-Bench: Evaluating LLMs as Multi-Turn Generative UI Assistants
abstract: Large language models can generate interactive web interfaces, but reliable generative UI requires maintaining an executable artifact as user requests evolve. We introduce EvoGenUI-Bench, a benchmark for multi-turn interface maintenance comprising 150 five-turn tasks and 750 turns across three scenarios: information presentation, executable interaction, and tool-grounded external state. We execute generated artifacts in a browser and evaluate them using screenshots, source and DOM evidence, actor traces, and runtime logs. Beyond turn-level and episode-level success, we measure cross-turn retention with Adjacent Pass Retention. Across eight models, even the strongest achieves 74.9% Turn Pass while completing only 37.3% of five-turn episodes; APR further falls to 52.4% on tool-grounded tasks. Diagnostic analysis shows that presentation failures center on information architecture, interaction failures on derived-state propagation and affordance binding, and tool-grounded failures additionally involve external-state grounding and requirement decomposition. These results reframe generative UI evaluation from judging isolated outputs to testing whether interface behavior, derived state, external state, and assistant claims remain synchronized as the artifact evolves.

title: Microseismic Weak Event Detection and First Arrival Picking Based on YOLOv8
abstract: Abstract：Weak event detection is a key step to improve the accuracy of first-arrival picking in microseismic monitoring.Traditional STA/LTA and AIC methods have limited detection capability under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions.This paper proposes a microseismic event detection method based on the YOLOv8 object detection model, which transforms event detection into a candidate-window object detection task.Experimental results show that YOLOv8 achieves an overall mAP50 of 0.948 on the test set, with a precision of 0.841, recall of 0.917, and mAP50 of 0.956 for weak events, and a false-detection rate of 0% on both types of negative samples.On this basis, a YOLOv8-detection-box-guided AIC joint first-arrival picking strategy is proposed.The detection box locates candidate event windows, within which the AIC function is computed for accurate picking, and multi-trace continuity constraints are further applied to improve the stability of the first-arrival picks.This method provides an effective technical solution for automated processing of low-SNR microseismic data.

title: Topology-Driven Parameter Optimization in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to neural network parameter optimization utilizing topology-driven methods. Traditional parameter optimization relies on fixed, predefined configurations, often resulting in suboptimal performance and limited generalization. We propose a method where the network's structure is dynamically shaped by a topological analysis of the input data, allowing for adaptation and improvement. This framework leverages a novel topological representation to guide the network's evolution, leading to enhanced generalization and robustness. The core mechanism centers around a continuous, evolving topology that dynamically adjusts the network's layer arrangements and connections, optimizing for a specific objective function. The paper presents a methodology for constructing and applying such a topology, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulated experiments and initial analysis of a simplified neural network architecture.

title: ##基于图卷积神经网络的知识图谱推理
abstract: This paper explores the application of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for knowledge graph reasoning. Traditional knowledge graph reasoning methods often rely on rule-based systems, which can be brittle and difficult to scale. We propose a novel approach that leverages the power of deep learning, specifically GCNs, to learn representations of nodes and predict relationships within a knowledge graph. The core claim of this work is that utilizing GCNs significantly improves both the accuracy and efficiency of knowledge graph reasoning. The mechanism involves representing the knowledge graph as a graph structure and employing GCNs for node representation learning and relationship prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a detailed analysis of the underlying mathematical framework and the potential for improved performance compared to conventional methods. The research contributes to a more robust and scalable approach to knowledge graph inference, offering a promising avenue for advancements in areas such as question answering, recommendation systems, and semantic understanding. ---
