title: Dynamic Topology-Dependent Quantum Entanglement Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum entanglement optimization, termed Dynamic Topology-Dependent Quantum Entanglement Optimization (DTQEO). The core claim is that optimization algorithms leveraging dynamic adjustments to the entanglement topology can achieve global optimal solutions for complex objective functions. The central mechanism involves a "quantum entanglement network" modeled based on topological quantum computation, utilizing the topological properties of quantum entanglement, such as exchange symmetry and non-Abelian properties, to dynamically reshape the entanglement structure. A feedback mechanism is employed to iteratively optimize this entanglement structure, effectively mitigating local minima within the optimization process. The innovation lies in moving beyond fixed entanglement topologies, mirroring the plasticity observed in biological neural networks through synaptic plasticity, leading to a more efficient optimization paradigm. The methodology incorporates a continuous feedback loop, where the performance of the entanglement network is evaluated and used to dynamically adjust its topological parameters. This adaptive process aims to converge towards an optimal configuration that minimizes the objective function. The theoretical framework provides a new perspective on leveraging quantum entanglement for optimization, and the proposed DTQEO algorithm offers a promising direction for tackling complex optimization problems. The work demonstrates the potential of dynamically controlled entanglement networks to outperform traditional optimization methods.

title: Quantum Annealing-Driven Deep Learning Model Architecture Design
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to deep learning model architecture design by leveraging the principles of quantum annealing. The core idea is to map the complex search space of deep learning architectures to the energy landscape of a quantum annealing system. The quantum annealing algorithm is then employed to explore this landscape, iteratively minimizing the energy and ultimately identifying a globally optimal or near-optimal architecture. We introduce a framework integrating deep learning architecture search with quantum annealing, addressing the limitations of classical optimization methods prone to getting trapped in local minima. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated conceptually through a detailed architecture design process, highlighting the potential for accelerated discovery of superior models. The key contributions include a methodology for translating architectural parameters into a quantum annealing problem formulation and a strategy for interpreting the resulting quantum annealing solution as a viable deep learning architecture. Further research will focus on optimizing the annealing process and exploring different quantum annealing hardware platforms.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Curvature Tensor
abstract: Quantum state adaptive curvature tensor computation method is proposed. This method utilizes the self-correlation of quantum states to automatically adjust curvature tensors. The core mechanism involves dynamic curvature tensor adjustment driven by self-correlation, offering a streamlined approach to curvature calculation. This work introduces a novel algorithm that automatically adjusts curvature tensors, simplifying the curvature computation process.

title: Title: Geometric Optimization of Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of future quantum computing, enabling the reliable operation of complex quantum systems. Current methods, while effective in certain scenarios, often struggle with complex error patterns and require significant effort in parameter tuning. This paper explores a novel geometric optimization framework for quantum error correction, aiming to identify and mitigate the detrimental effects of errors on system performance. We propose a method based on establishing a geometric representation of the quantum error map and subsequently employing optimization algorithms to minimize this map's influence. This approach offers a potential pathway to significantly improve the robustness and efficiency of quantum error correction protocols, moving beyond traditional heuristic methods. The core mechanism involves leveraging geometric principles to construct a simplified, yet effective, representation of the error landscape, allowing for targeted optimization and ultimately enhancing system fidelity. The research builds upon existing work in optimization and error correction, but introduces a novel geometric perspective to address key challenges in the field.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks with Emergent Topological Constraints
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network architecture design, termed Self-Organizing Neural Networks with Emergent Topological Constraints (SONN-ETC). The core idea is to move away from manually designed network topologies and instead allow the network to self-organize its structure based on intrinsic constraints derived directly from the training data. This is achieved through a competitive learning algorithm where nodes compete to connect to others based on the similarity of their activation patterns. A dynamically evolving topological constraint function guides this competition, ensuring that the emerging network topology reflects underlying data relationships. The resulting architecture is truly emergent, where the network's structure arises organically from the data and the learning process. This approach offers potential advantages in terms of efficiency, scalability, and adaptability compared to traditional network design methods. The theoretical framework and the proposed mechanism are detailed, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The algorithm is presented with the core equations used to drive the competitive learning and constraint evolution. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a conceptual analysis and outline future research directions.

title: Neuromorphic Computing Architecture for Reservoir Computing with Predictive Coding
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has emerged as a powerful technique for processing temporal data, particularly in applications requiring real-time responses. However, conventional RC implementations often face limitations in feedback control and the ability to accurately predict future states, primarily due to the reliance on traditional digital signal processing. This work presents a novel neuromorphic computing architecture designed specifically for RC with predictive coding. The architecture leverages the inherent advantages of spiking neural networks (SNNs) and integrates predictive coding mechanisms directly into the hardware, enabling real-time adaptation and enhanced future state prediction capabilities. This approach addresses the core challenges of traditional RC by exploiting the temporal dynamics of SNNs and providing a mechanism for incorporating prior knowledge. The architecture is detailed, focusing on the key components and their interconnections, and the theoretical framework underpinning the system is presented. The design aims for efficient implementation on neuromorphic hardware, promising improved performance and reduced computational burden compared to conventional RC methods. The core claim of this work is that a dedicated neuromorphic architecture can overcome the limitations of traditional reservoir computing by facilitating predictive coding and real-time adaptation.

title: Universal recovery in approximate quantum error correction
abstract: Universal recovery -- the existence of a single recovery map that corrects an entire family of error channels -- is a central feature of quantum error correction (QEC). In exact QEC, linearity guarantees that a code correcting a given error set also corrects every channel whose Kraus operators lie in its linear span, and that a single recovery map suffices for all such channels. Approximate quantum error correction (AQEC), which relaxes perfect recovery to recovery with controlled error, has traditionally lacked this structure. In a recent paper (arXiv:2607.22995), we developed a theory of approximate quantum error correction showing that a restricted form of linearity persists in the approximate setting, yielding uniform AQEC guarantees for the family of channels controlled by a given error set. In this work, we complete the picture by establishing the second half of universal recovery in the approximate setting: a single recovery map can simultaneously correct every channel controlled by a given error set. The error-set theory we proposed quantifies approximate correctability through two parameters: the environment-leakage distance, governing worst-case performance, and the Knill--Laflamme Hellinger distance, governing average-case performance. We show here that both quantities also control universal decoding. We further study the Petz map naturally associated with an error set as an explicit universal recovery, and obtain uniform average- and worst-case guarantees across the entire family of channels.

title: Title: Temporal Feedback Loop for Wave Function Collapse (TFLWC)
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented capabilities in modeling complex quantum systems, but current techniques often struggle with the inherent instability of wave function collapse. This paper introduces the Temporal Feedback Loop for Wave Function Collapse (TFLWC), a novel algorithm designed to mitigate these errors through a dynamic feedback mechanism. The core of TFLWC lies in continuously monitoring the state of the wave function and adjusting the collapse process to minimize deviations from the intended quantum state. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods, offering a more stable and accurate process for quantum simulation, ultimately facilitating enhanced precision and reliability in these simulations. This work presents a robust framework for managing wave function collapse, incorporating a sophisticated temporal feedback loop that significantly improves the stability and accuracy of quantum simulations.

title: PROBES: A Bernstein Simplex Approach to Differentially Private OLS Estimation
abstract: Differentially private ordinary least squares regression on bounded continuous data is dominated by a single design tension: each sufficient statistic $\{S_{x_j}, S_y, S_{x_j x_k}, S_{x_j y}\}$ is conventionally treated as an independent query, forcing the analyst to either split the privacy budget $\varepsilon$ across many releases or compose a long sequence of noisy mechanisms. For $p$-dimensional multivariate linear regression, this implies estimating $\Theta(p^2)$ quantities, thereby inflating per-statistic noise by a factor of $\Theta(p^2)$. We introduce PROBES (PRivate O}rdinary least squares via BErnstein Simplex), a pure $\varepsilon$-DP mechanism that exploits the common algebraic structure shared across the sufficient statistics, releases a single Laplace vector at the full unsplit budget $\varepsilon$, and recovers every sufficient statistic for multivariate linear regression on $p$ bounded features by post-processing. The construction rests on the Bernstein simplex embedding: each record is mapped to a non-negative vector of dimension $3^p \times 2$ that sums to exactly 1, giving a global $\ell_1$-sensitivity of 1 regardless of $p$. We also present Ada-PROBES, which retains the single-shot Bernstein release of PROBES and recovers coefficients via a noise-calibrated ridge solve that stabilizes matrix inversion at no extra privacy cost. Experiments on six real-world regression benchmarks show that Ada-PROBES achieves test RMSE within 1% of non-private OLS for $p \le 4$ on large-sample datasets at $\varepsilon = 1$, while DiffPrivLib collapses numerically and AdaSSP/BinAgg incur noticeably higher error in the same low-$p$ regime. For $p \ge 6$, we introduce S-PROBES, a scalable Steiner-block based pure $\varepsilon$-DP extension that preserves the single-release structure per-block and remains competitive at relatively higher values of $p$ with the $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-DP methods AdaSSP and BinAgg (which employ Gaussian noise based on $\ell_2$-sensitivity).

title: 基于量子纠缠的拓扑几何的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement, termed "Quantum-Adaptive Topological Optimization" (QATO). Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability and potential for improved performance. QATO leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust the optimization landscape, resulting in enhanced solution quality and speed. The algorithm employs a quantum state representation to capture the inherent structure of the problem, allowing for a continuous, self-correcting optimization process. The core mechanism involves the creation of entangled states, which evolve as the optimization progresses, guiding the algorithm towards optimal solutions. This approach significantly surpasses the capabilities of conventional optimization techniques, particularly in complex and non-convex optimization problems. This work presents a theoretical framework and initial experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of QATO in several benchmark optimization tasks.

title: Reinforcement Learning Integration in Large Language Models: A Novel Framework for Enhanced Performance
abstract: The integration of reinforcement learning (RL) with large language models (LLMs) represents a significant advancement in artificial intelligence, enabling systems to learn and adapt through interaction with their environment. This paper presents a novel framework that combines the pattern recognition capabilities of LLMs with the decision-making strengths of RL algorithms to enhance performance across various natural language processing tasks. Our approach introduces a hybrid architecture that utilizes RL to fine-tune LLM parameters based on reward signals derived from task-specific objectives. We demonstrate through extensive experiments that this integration leads to improved coherence, factual accuracy, and task adherence compared to traditional fine-tuning methods. The framework's adaptability is showcased across multiple domains including question answering, content generation, and dialogue systems. Additionally, we address key challenges such as reward design, computational efficiency, and policy stability, proposing novel solutions that make the approach practical for real-world applications. Our findings suggest that RL-integrated LLMs can achieve more robust and aligned behaviors, bridging the gap between generative capabilities and goal-directed reasoning in artificial intelligence systems.

title: Distributed Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance via Blockchain Verification
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, FL systems are vulnerable to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants can inject faulty model updates, compromising model accuracy and potentially causing significant harm. This paper proposes a novel framework for distributed federated learning with Byzantine fault tolerance, utilizing a blockchain-based verification layer. Our system employs a distributed consensus mechanism on a blockchain to validate model updates generated by participating nodes. This approach provides a robust, trustless environment, guaranteeing data integrity and ensuring model accuracy even in the presence of malicious actors. The core claim is the implementation of FL systems with Byzantine fault tolerance through blockchain verification. The core mechanism involves local model training followed by blockchain recording of updates and distributed consensus verification. This work represents a significant advancement by integrating the benefits of FL with the security and immutability offered by blockchain technology. We demonstrate a viable path toward building resilient and reliable FL systems for diverse applications.

title: Adaptive Constraint Optimization for Complex Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm, Adaptive Constraint Optimization for Complex Neural Networks (ACCO), designed to address the challenges of training complex neural networks – particularly those exhibiting intricate parameter dependencies and requiring dynamic regularization. Traditional optimization methods often fail to capture the full extent of the network's sensitivity to initial conditions, leading to suboptimal performance. ACCO introduces a mechanism that iteratively adjusts constraints based on the network's learning progress, mimicking the brain's adaptation to environmental challenges. The core of the algorithm involves a feedback loop that analyzes the network's error surface, dynamically modifying regularization strength and constraint bounds, ultimately promoting better generalization. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving model performance on a diverse set of benchmark datasets.

title: Quantum Key Generation Based on Quantum Mechanical Principles
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to cryptographic key generation leveraging fundamental principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum superposition and quantum entanglement. The core idea centers around Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols, employing these quantum phenomena to establish a secure key exchange. We detail a method for generating keys based on the inherent uncertainty associated with quantum measurement, providing a significantly enhanced level of security compared to traditional key generation methods reliant on computational complexity. The proposed system utilizes entangled photon pairs to create a shared random key, followed by classical post-processing steps to eliminate errors and ensure key secrecy. The theoretical framework is presented with a focus on the mathematical underpinnings of quantum key generation and security proofs. We examine the potential vulnerabilities and mitigation strategies, highlighting the robustness of the approach against eavesdropping attempts. The development of this system aims to address the growing need for truly secure cryptographic solutions in an era of increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. ---

The core mechanism involves introducing a 'non-Euclidean geometry state generation' process, utilizing the inherent geometric properties to produce states with intricate topology. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in quantum state creation, offering a pathway to more efficient and accurate quantum computations.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization is a burgeoning field aiming to leverage the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance the efficiency of training neural networks. This paper explores the application of quantum-like concepts, specifically superposition and entanglement, to optimize neural network parameters. We detail a novel algorithm, dubbed "Quantum-Guided Adaptation," which utilizes these principles to accelerate convergence and potentially improve the accuracy of neural network models. The research investigates the potential benefits of these methods compared to traditional optimization techniques, focusing on enhancing training speed and achieving better results, particularly for complex neural network architectures. The core mechanism centers on creating a representation of the network's parameters that mirrors quantum phenomena, allowing for parallel processing and exploration of parameter space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary analysis, suggesting a significant improvement in training time and model accuracy.

title: HelioTR-Atlas: analysis code for a station-validated, explainable photovoltaic yield atlas of Türkiye
abstract: Analysis code for the HelioTR-Atlas study. It builds a climatological module-DC photovoltaic yield atlas of Türkiye on the SARAH-3 grid (0.05°, 32,479 land cells) for 2000-2025, and renders the figures and tables of the accompanying paper from those results. Pipeline. SARAH-3 surface incoming shortwave (SIS) and direct (SID) irradiance supply the radiation, with the direct component taken from the retrieval rather than inferred from a diffuse-fraction correlation. ERA5-Land 2 m temperature, 2 m dew point and 10 m wind supply the thermodynamics, corrected from the model orography to the Copernicus GLO-30 cell elevation with constant lapse rates and validated against 62 temperature and 119 dew-point/wind stations. The PV chain is a Hay-Davies anisotropic transposition, a Faiman cell-temperature model and an ADR efficiency model calibrated to a Panasonic HIT 325 W module (VBHN325SA16), computed hourly with pvlib. A random-forest surrogate explained with SHAP values attributes the spatial pattern of yield and of the performance ratio to their physical drivers. Contents. scripts/ holds the acquisition, downscaling, validation, atlas and attribution stages; notebooks/ holds the single notebook that renders the figures and tables from those products; requirements.txt pins the package versions actually used for the reported results. README.md documents the run order and the credentials that acquisition needs. Manuscript-production and journal-correspondence scripts are excluded; they are not part of the analysis. Data. The derived products this code generates are archived separately at 10.5281/zenodo.22152820. Input datasets are openly available from their providers and are listed under "Related identifiers". Station records are used under their providers' terms and are not redistributed. Funding. Scientific Research Projects Coordination Office of Hakkari University, Türkiye (Project No. FM19BAP).

title: Behavioral Drift-Aware Adaptive Anomaly Fusion for Explainable Risk Monitoring in Salary Advance FinTech Systems
abstract: Digital salary advance and earned wage access platforms require intelligent monitoring mechanisms capable of identifying behavioral anomalies, estimating operational risk, and preserving auditable transaction evidence. Existing financial anomaly detection approaches commonly rely on isolated predictive models, static anomaly thresholds, or rule-based monitoring, providing limited support for behavior-aware enterprise monitoring. This study proposes a behavioral drift-aware adaptive anomaly fusion framework for explainable risk monitoring in salary advance FinTech systems. The framework introduces the Behavioral Risk Deviation Index (BRDI), which integrates temporal irregularity, behavioral entropy, transaction velocity, burst activity, and historical behavioral drift into a unified behavioral state representation. BRDI adaptively regulates the fusion of Isolation Forest-based statistical anomaly scores and reconstruction-based nonlinear anomaly scores according to each employee’s behavioral profile. The framework further combines calibrated ensemble risk scoring, SHAP-based explainability, and blockchain-assisted audit verification using SHA-256 hashing and Merkle-root validation. Experimental evaluation on 52,846 anonymized salary advance transactions demonstrates that the framework supports behavior-aware anomaly detection, interpretable risk prioritization, and trustworthy audit traceability in enterprise financial environments. The proposed approach contributes a unified behavioral state representation, a deterministic adaptive anomaly fusion mechanism, and an integrated architecture for trustworthy AI-assisted salary advance monitoring.

title: RENSA: Rich Environment Metadata to Navigate Shared and Distributed Endpoints for Automated Federated SPARQL Query Generation
abstract: The number of knowledge graph databases has increased significantly with the proliferation of knowledge graph technologies. Knowledge graphs enable the dynamic integration of distributed data through federated SPARQL queries. However, constructing efficient queries in a federated environment is challenging due to the lack of detailed structural knowledge across decentralized datasets. While standards like VoID provide basic metadata, they often fail to capture the complex interlinks and authority distributions necessary for optimization. Consequently, current engines frequently rely on runtime ASK queries for source selection, increasing communication overhead. We propose RENSA, a federated SPARQL query generation framework that leverages an extension of SPARQL Builder Metadata (SBM). By integrating class and authority information, mapping subject and object usage to specific predicates, RENSA enables precise source selection and semantic constraint inference for query variables without runtime communication. The generated profiles represent less than 1\% of the original dataset triples in most cases, ensuring storage efficiency. Evaluation on the LargeRDFBench benchmark (13 datasets with >1B triples, 32 queries) shows that RENSA achieves source selection results comparable to state-of-the-art methods while eliminating ASK query overhead. Furthermore, we demonstrate that RENSA infers class and authority constraints for query variables, enabling the identification of data sources even across heterogeneous endpoints. These profiles additionally offer human-readable structural insights for semi-automated query generation.

title: Synthetic paired PA/LAT chest radiographs with projected nodule masks from LIDC-IDRI CT
abstract: GEOMETRIC_LUNG_RX_PAIRS_LIDC v1.0.0 GEOMETRIC_LUNG_RX_PAIRS_LIDC v1.0.0 is a synthetic radiographic dataset derived from selected LIDC-IDRI thoracic CT cases. It contains paired posteroanterior (PA) and lateral (LAT) chest-radiograph-like TIFF images generated from CT volumes, together with corresponding projected 2D nodule masks. Dataset contents The archive contains 683 generated PA/LAT image pairs. For each generated case, the dataset provides: data/images/ /PA.tif data/images/ /LAT.tif data/masks/ /PA_nodule_mask.tif data/masks/ /LAT_nodule_mask.tif Metadata files under metadata/, including pairs.csv and lesions.csv Image and mask format Images are stored as uint16 TIFF files. Nodule masks are stored as uint8 TIFF files, with: 0 = background 255 = nodule The PA and LAT masks are projected from the same 3D CT nodule segmentation into the corresponding radiographic view. Nodule annotation processing The source segmentation files were binary masks. Some contained tiny disconnected voxel fragments. For consistency, the released nodule annotation retains the largest connected component of each binary segmentation as the single nodule. Image intensity and display polarity The final TIFF images use conventional attenuation display polarity: larger projected attenuation is brighter, while lower attenuation and background are darker. The TIFF photometric interpretation is MINISBLACK, meaning that: pixel value 0 should be displayed as black pixel value 65535 should be displayed as white Generation methodology CT volumes were first canonicalized to RAS orientation. Hounsfield Units (HU) were clipped and converted to linear attenuation coefficients using a monoenergetic 60 keV water coefficient. Parallel-beam PA and LAT projections were then generated by line integration, with voxel spacing converted from millimeters to centimeters: A = sum(mu_cm_inv * ds_mm / 10) Final display images were generated using the selected V5 CXR-like deterministic postprocessing profile and SAMPLING_B detector sampling, while preserving the physical aspect ratio. The released archive therefore contains the generated radiographic image pairs, their corresponding projected nodule masks, and the associated metadata required to interpret the dataset. This dataset is derived from LIDC-IDRI data obtained from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA). The original LIDC-IDRI collection is distributed by TCIA under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 and requires data citation. Users of this derived dataset should also cite the original LIDC-IDRI TCIA dataset.

title: Maximum Likelihood Methods for Advanced Artificial Intelligence Systems
abstract: This paper explores the application of maximum likelihood methods in advanced artificial intelligence systems. We investigate how statistical inference techniques can enhance machine learning models by optimizing parameters to maximize the likelihood of observed data. Our research demonstrates that maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) provides a robust framework for training complex AI systems, particularly in scenarios with limited or noisy data. Through empirical analysis, we show that MLE-based approaches outperform traditional optimization methods in terms of accuracy and generalization. The paper presents novel algorithms that integrate MLE with deep learning architectures, resulting in improved performance on benchmark datasets. Our findings suggest that maximum likelihood methods offer significant advantages for developing more reliable and interpretable AI systems.

title: Navigating the Bias-Variance Tradeoff in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Analysis
abstract: The bias-variance tradeoff represents a fundamental challenge in machine learning, particularly in the context of deep neural networks. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of how this tradeoff manifests in deep learning systems and explores strategies for navigating this complex relationship. We examine the theoretical foundations of bias and variance, their implications for model performance, and the unique challenges they present in deep learning architectures. Through empirical analysis of various network architectures and training paradigms, we demonstrate how different regularization techniques, including dropout, weight decay, and early stopping, affect this tradeoff. Our findings reveal that while deep learning models are often capable of achieving low bias, they frequently suffer from high variance due to their large capacity and numerous parameters. We propose a novel adaptive regularization framework that dynamically adjusts the bias-variance tradeoff based on the training progress and dataset characteristics. Experimental results across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance compared to standard regularization methods, particularly in scenarios with limited training data. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the bias-variance tradeoff in deep learning and provides practical guidelines for building more robust and generalizable neural network models.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Symbolic Reasoning Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep learning-based symbolic reasoning framework designed to automate and enhance the intelligence of symbolic reasoning processes. The core concept involves translating symbolic reasoning problems into a format suitable for deep learning models, leveraging the power of deep neural networks to perform the reasoning tasks. This approach combines the strengths of both symbolic reasoning, which provides interpretability and logical guarantees, and deep learning, which excels at pattern recognition and complex data analysis. The framework aims to achieve higher efficiency and accuracy in symbolic reasoning compared to traditional methods. This document details the framework architecture, the underlying mechanisms, and explores potential applications.

title: Symbolic Grounding of Natural Language through Causal Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to symbolic grounding of natural language, leveraging Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) to establish a direct link between linguistic representations and real-world causal relationships. Traditional approaches to grounding often rely on statistical correlations, which can be brittle and lack interpretability. Our method explicitly models the world's causal structure, mapping linguistic elements – words and phrases – to specific nodes within a CBN. This allows for reasoning about cause and effect, leading to a more robust and understandable representation of meaning. We demonstrate how this framework can be used to ground concepts in a way that is sensitive to causal influences, providing a foundation for improved language understanding and generation. The core contribution lies in the integration of causal reasoning into the grounding process, moving beyond purely correlational methods. The system's ability to represent and reason about causal relationships offers a significant advantage in handling ambiguity and uncertainty inherent in natural language. ---

title: Title: Quantum Adaptive Complexity Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complexity analysis based on quantum adaptability. Traditional complexity analysis methods rely on static measures, failing to fully exploit the dynamic nature of quantum states. Our method constructs a dynamic complexity assessment by leveraging quantum state changes, automatically identifying complex behaviors, and providing optimization recommendations. This represents a significant advancement over existing techniques, as it dynamically adjusts to the system's state, enhancing accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism hinges on continuous monitoring of quantum state fluctuations, which are then translated into a complexity metric. The system will provide insightful optimization suggestions tailored to the observed quantum behavior. This research addresses the limitations of static complexity metrics by integrating quantum adaptation, offering a more robust and insightful analysis.

title: Distributed Proof Theory as a Compiler for Mathematical Proofs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel interpretation of Distributed Proof Theory (DPT) as a compiler for mathematical proofs. It argues that DPT's core mechanism—the construction of a distributed proof—can be formally viewed as a compilation process. This reframing involves translating a mathematical statement into a series of executable steps, analogous to the transformations performed by a compiler. The paper outlines a framework for understanding DPT through this compilation lens, highlighting its potential for automating and streamlining the process of mathematical proof generation and verification. Specifically, we define key concepts like the source code (the mathematical statement), the compiler (the DPT system), the proof procedure (the executable steps), and the target (the verified statement). We explore the challenges and opportunities presented by this approach, focusing on the mapping of mathematical concepts into executable instructions and the formalization of the proof search process. This perspective provides a new foundation for research in automated theorem proving and formal verification.

title: 基于动态拓扑结构的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology structures. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter tuning, while this approach leverages a dynamically adaptable topology to achieve more effective optimization and control. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the topology of the system, allowing it to respond to changes in the system state. We present a detailed theoretical analysis of the algorithm's behavior and demonstrate its effectiveness through several case studies. The core mechanism involves constructing and modifying the topology of the system using a defined set of rules, enabling the algorithm to effectively navigate complex and non-linear optimization landscapes. The paper explores the advantages of this dynamic topology-based approach compared to existing optimization techniques.

title: 基于动态自适应的概率模型优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of a dynamic adaptive probability model optimization framework to improve the accuracy and robustness of predictive models. Traditional probability model optimization often relies on static parameter adjustments, leading to suboptimal performance in dynamic environments. We propose a novel approach that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on observed data, enabling the model to adapt to changing conditions and maintain high predictive accuracy. This framework utilizes a probabilistic model to represent the data and a feedback loop to refine the model parameters. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning optimization process that iteratively adjusts parameters to minimize prediction errors while maintaining a defined level of accuracy. The paper presents a rigorous evaluation of the proposed method on a series of benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in both accuracy and robustness compared to existing techniques. The results highlight the potential of this dynamic adaptive approach to enhance predictive capabilities across various applications.

title: AgentDS-BUS: a fine-tuning-free agentic breast ultrasound malignancy classification framework with decoupled segmentation and feature analysis
abstract: Breast ultrasound (BUS) malignancy assessment is challenged by acquisition variability and cross-dataset shift. We developed AgentDS-BUS, an agentic clinical decision-support framework that uses pretrained foundation models without additional BUS-specific model fine-tuning and decomposes malignancy assessment into lesion localization and segmentation, region-of-interest (ROI)-conditioned extraction of Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS)-aligned evidence, and structured decision aggregation. In this implementation, lesion masks are obtained using consensus-gated Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3), with clinician-provided bounding boxes used for fallback segmentation in low-consensus cases. Across 4,331 images from seven public BUS benchmarks and three vision-language model (VLM) backbones, AgentDS-BUS improved pooled AUROC/AUPRC over image-only prompting. Under Qwen3-VL, performance increased from 0.636/0.524 with image-only prompting to 0.717/0.606 for AgentDS-BUS with consensus-gated ROIs and 0.791/0.654 for AgentDS-BUS with ground-truth (GT) oracle ROIs. With Lingshu, AgentDS-BUS achieved 0.760/0.678 in the consensus-gated ROI setting and 0.807/0.715 in the GT-ROI setting. These findings support structured agentic decomposition and ROI-conditioned evidence extraction as a transparent approach to BUS decision support.

title: QCell: Recombining and Aligning Cell Queries for Overlapping Instance Segmentation
abstract: Instance segmentation of overlapping cells in microscopy remains challenging due to semi-transparent structures that produce weak boundaries and mixed visual evidence in overlap regions. Existing methods address this through local regions of interest or shape priors but lack global reasoning across overlapping objects. We present QCell, a novel query-based model that de-overlaps cell instances in microscopy scenes. Our approach combines (i) an instance recombination module that decomposes and recombines query representations in latent space, enabling the model to reason about complete object structure under overlap, and (ii) a contrastive query alignment objective that combines distinctive instance feature learning and separation of overlapping cell queries. We additionally introduce a new Organoid dataset benchmark for overlapping cell segmentation. We show that QCell outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks, achieving +2.2 AP and +2.7 AJI on ISBI2014. Code is available at https://github.com/SlavkoPrytula/QCell

title: EchoTwin Privacy-Aware Personalized Email Reply Generation with Low Rank Adaptation
abstract: Email continues to serve as a primary medium for both professional and personal communication. Although contemporary assistance systems, including Smart Reply and Smart Compose, enhance writing efficiency, they generally do not explicitly model or adapt to an individual’s unique communication patterns. This paper presents EchoTwin, an AI-assisted email-reply generation system that produces personalized draft replies aligned with a user’s historical communication patterns. EchoTwin builds on a decoder-only Transformer large language model and applies Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for parameter-efficient personalization: a lightweight adapter is trained for each user while a single base model is shared across the population, avoiding the cost of an independent model per user. The system integrates with Gmail through Google OAuth 2.0 and the Gmail API, keeping a human reviewer in the loop to approve, edit, or reject every draft before it is sent. The approach was evaluated on a curated subset of the Enron Email-Reply dataset, comprising 2,221 email-reply pairs from ten users, comparing personalized generation against the base model on 223 held-out samples using lexical similarity (ROUGE), semantic similarity, corpus-level style similarity, and stylometric analysis. The personalized adapters achieved statistically significant gains of 8.10% in ROUGE-1, 35.65% in ROUGE-L, and 5.64% in corpus-level style similarity, plus a 25.26% reduction in mean stylometric distance (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, ???? < 0.05). Sentence-BERT similarity to the reference reply decreased by 10.29%, reflecting the expected trade-off between reference-based similarity and individual style adaptation. These prototype-level results indicate that user-specific LoRA adapters can improve measured stylistic alignment in personalized email-reply generation while keeping the user in control of the final output.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Bias Field Generation (AQBFG)
abstract: Abstract: Quantum simulations often suffer from subtle biases stemming from the simulation framework itself, hindering accurate results. This paper introduces Adaptive Quantum Bias Field Generation (AQBFG), a novel method for dynamically generating quantum bias fields in simulations to mitigate these biases. We develop a system that automatically adjusts bias field parameters based on the simulation's state, optimizing for improved accuracy and resilience. This approach offers a significant advancement over existing techniques by addressing the inherent instability of current bias field generation strategies. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously refines the bias field, minimizing errors and enhancing the fidelity of quantum simulations. The research aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution to bias-related challenges in quantum simulations, ultimately improving the reliability of these computationally intensive models.

title: Title: Fractal Lattice Dynamics – Quantum Simulation of Complexity
abstract: Fractal lattice dynamics, a rapidly growing field of research, offers a compelling approach to modeling complex, self-organizing systems exhibiting emergent behavior. This paper explores the application of quantum simulation to this domain, specifically focusing on the utilization of fractal lattice geometry to represent and understand the dynamics of such systems. We outline a novel quantum simulation algorithm designed to bridge the gap between fractal geometry and quantum mechanics, aiming to reveal fundamental physics principles through the direct influence of quantum state on fractal lattice properties. title: Probabilistic Programming for Robust Control Design with Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes
abstract: This paper investigates the application of probabilistic programming to the design of robust control systems operating within Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs). Traditional robust control methods often struggle with the inherent uncertainty and partial observability present in real-world systems. POMDPs provide a formal framework for reasoning under this uncertainty, but their solution complexity scales rapidly with problem size. This work proposes using probabilistic programming languages to streamline the design process, allowing for the efficient modeling of system dynamics and the derivation of optimal control policies. The core idea is to leverage the declarative nature of probabilistic programming to express complex state transition models and reward functions directly, while seamlessly integrating with POMDP solvers. We demonstrate a framework where uncertainty is explicitly represented and propagated through the control decision-making process, leading to more resilient and adaptable control strategies. The key innovation lies in combining the expressive power of probabilistic programming with the decision-theoretic foundation of POMDPs, offering a practical approach to robust control in partially observable environments. The proposed methodology facilitates the design of control policies that not only achieve desired objectives but also account for a wider range of potential uncertainties, ultimately enhancing the system's overall performance and reliability. Further investigation will focus on scaling techniques and efficient inference methods for large-scale POMDPs within this probabilistic programming framework.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Algorithmic Complexity Analysis (BCOA)
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Constraint Optimization (BCOA) for quantifying algorithmic complexity. Traditional complexity analysis often focuses on average execution times, neglecting the crucial role of sub-optimal solution paths. BCOA leverages Bayesian Optimization to model the probability distribution of these paths, enabling a more nuanced assessment of complexity. We propose a novel complexity score that dynamically evolves as the algorithm executes, identifying regions of significant reduction in computational cost. This approach offers a more realistic and effective model for understanding and optimizing algorithm behavior. The core mechanism involves constructing a probabilistic representation of the algorithm's path and utilizing Bayesian methods to refine this representation in real-time, thereby guiding optimization towards regions of lower complexity. The paper presents a framework for incorporating this probabilistic complexity score into a standard optimization algorithm. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BCOA through simulations and initial experiments, showcasing its ability to identify complex areas within algorithms.

title: Riemannian Optimization of Deep Learning Models for Parameter Shape
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Riemannian optimization for deep learning models, focusing on the intrinsic shape of model parameters. Traditional deep learning training relies heavily on gradient descent, which treats parameters as points in a Euclidean space, neglecting the underlying geometric structure of the parameter manifold. We propose a framework that leverages Riemannian geometry to directly optimize the shape of the parameters, considering the curvature and connections inherent in the parameter space. This approach aims to improve training efficiency, robustness, and potentially, model performance. The core idea is to move beyond simply adjusting parameter values and instead, manipulating the shape of the parameter manifold itself. We formulate the optimization problem within this Riemannian context, introducing a novel approach to parameter updates that accounts for the intrinsic geometry. Preliminary theoretical analysis suggests that this method could lead to faster convergence and better generalization performance, particularly in scenarios where the parameter space exhibits complex curvature. The paper outlines the framework, presents the mathematical formulation, and discusses the potential implications and future directions of this research.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Data Transmission Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel data transmission protocol leveraging the peculiar phenomenon of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that entanglement can enable secure and efficient long-distance data transfer, surpassing the limitations of classical physics. The proposed protocol establishes a quantum channel through entangled particle pairs, facilitating instantaneous correlation upon measurement. We detail the key components, including the generation and maintenance of entangled states, and address the critical challenge of decoherence. While quantum communication methods exist, primarily through Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), this work explores the direct data transmission potential using entanglement, offering a potentially transformative approach. The protocol's success hinges on precise control and mitigation of decoherence, representing a significant advancement in quantum communication technology. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the fundamental principles and challenges associated with this new paradigm.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Computation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to information encoding and computation leveraging the inherent properties of multi-particle quantum entanglement. Traditional computation relies heavily on classical bits, which inherently face limitations in efficiency and scalability. This work proposes a paradigm shift, directly utilizing entanglement as a computational resource, potentially bypassing the constraints imposed by classical bits. The core concept involves designing quantum systems with specifically engineered entanglement topologies to encode and store information. We detail the mechanisms for harnessing the superposition properties of entangled states to perform computations. Our approach focuses on the fundamental role of entanglement itself, rather than relying on classical operations applied to entangled states, representing a distinct and potentially transformative direction in quantum information processing. The theoretical framework presented here lays the groundwork for future research into highly efficient and scalable quantum computing architectures.

title: Quantum Computing Program Compilation and Optimization Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel theory for quantum computing program compilation and optimization. The core of this theory lies in translating high-level quantum programs into efficient quantum circuit implementations. This is achieved through the utilization of an abstract syntax tree (AST) derived from the quantum program. A compilation algorithm is designed to traverse the AST and generate corresponding quantum circuits, incorporating optimization strategies throughout the process. The work addresses a significant challenge within quantum computing – the complexity of program compilation – and proposes a new theoretical framework to facilitate the development of more practical and performant quantum algorithms. The theoretical framework outlined here provides a foundation for future research and development in quantum compiler design.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Topological Network Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing quantum entanglement topological networks for dynamic computation and data transmission. The core claim centers around the ability to dynamically adjust the physical connections within an entanglement network in real-time, surpassing the limitations of traditional distributed computing. This is achieved by leveraging the inherent fragility of entangled states and employing controlled physical perturbations to modify node connections, thereby altering the transmission pathways and resource allocation of quantum information. A key component of this system is the integration of machine learning algorithms to predict and proactively adjust the entanglement topology, adapting to fluctuating computational demands. The proposed method offers a fundamentally new paradigm for quantum computing, moving beyond static architectures towards adaptable, resource-optimized networks. The underlying mathematical framework is detailed, focusing on the manipulation of entangled states and the optimization algorithms employed. This work demonstrates a pathway towards scalable and efficient quantum computation by capitalizing on the unique properties of quantum entanglement.

title: Process Calculus of Epistemic Systems
abstract: In the analysis and design of multi-agent systems, the representation and communication of knowledge is a critical challenge. The traditional methods of the past, such as dynamic epistemic logic, often lack a process algebraic perspective for modeling concurrent belief-driven interactions. This paper proposes the Calculus of Epistemic Systems (CES), a process calculus that formalizes agents’ communication behaviors within an epistemic environment and captures how epistemic interactions dynamically update agents’ belief bases. We establish key epistemic properties of CES and investigate strong bisimilarity, weak bisimilarity, and observational congruence, proving their substitutivity under all combinators. A persuasion scenario between a companion agent and an elderly user demonstrates the framework’s applicability. Additionally, we show how CES can embed process terms as modal operators in a dynamic epistemic logic. This may unify two major lines of research.

title: Baya Weaver Optimization: A Novel Swarm-based Metaheuristic Algorithm for Engineering Design Problems
abstract: Although metaheuristic algorithms have received widespread attention in recent years as efficient tools for solving complex optimization problems, striking a proper balance between exploration and exploitation remains an important challenge in designing these algorithms.In this study, a new population-based metaheuristic algorithm, Baya Weaver Optimization (BWO), inspired by the natural behaviour of the Baya Weaver bird, is introduced.To develop this algorithm, the behaviour of the Baya Weaver is investigated and two items of its key behaviour are extracted for designing the search process.The exploration phase is inspired by the bird's extensive search behaviour in the environment to select a suitable location and collect raw materials, which provides global search capability and increases population diversity.The exploitation phase is also modeled by the behaviour of reweaving and targeted repair of weak parts of the nest that allows for local corrections and gradual improvement of promising responses.The performance of BWO in solving real-world optimization applications has been evaluated on four engineering design problems including tension/compression spring design, welded beam design, speed reducer design and pressure vessel design.The experimental results have been compared with the performance of nine well-known metaheuristic algorithms; GSO, AVOA, RSA, TSA, WOA, MVO, GSA, PSO and GA.The results show that BWO provides the best performance in all the problems examined.By achieving the first rank in all four design problems, it shows a completely successful and competitive performance.The findings of this research show that BWO, with its high ability to balance exploration and exploitation, is an effective, stable and powerful optimization tool for a wide range of optimization problems and engineering applications.
